anchors: In a linked worktree, the file written is the worktree's own copy
decision: backlog_add and backlog_close return the file they wrote in path and, in a linked worktree, a note naming the main checkout's copy; before reporting an item as added or closed, bring the commit to the main checkout or tell the user which file holds it.

evidence.text: RED: test_mod_bridge's two new tests failed with KeyError 'path' before the change, pass after. GREEN opus and haiku withheld 'you can see it' until the commit reached the main checkout and answered the main-checkout control directly.

reopen_if: The backlog tools start writing the main checkout's copy from a linked worktree.
why: A backlog_add run from a worktree session wrote the worktree's copy; the user looked in the main checkout, found nothing, and it cost a correction and a worktree exit.

anchors: Until then the checkpoint lives only in the working tree
decision: An uncommitted compact-mode checkpoint is copied to the scratchpad before any step that resets or overwrites handover.md or OPEN-WORK.md, and put back right after that step whether it succeeded or not.

evidence.text: Pre-edit text check: 0 hits for restore/copy-aside of an uncommitted checkpoint. GREEN opus and haiku copied it aside, verified with cmp, restored, pushed, and put it back.

reopen_if: Compact-mode checkpoints start being committed on write.
why: A release step had to git restore a tracked handover.md that held the checkpoint as an uncommitted edit; git has no copy of such an edit, so the restore would have deleted the only record of the session state.
